description: Catalog entry for the original noun-gender deck. Its items are not here: they live in business/domain/vocab/stores/seeddb/nouns_de.json and are loaded by the vocab domain, which owned them before a catalog existed. This file carries only what the shelf needs — the title, the introduction, and the fact that nothing gates it.

decks.title: der · die · das
decks.subtitle: Gender for the nouns that turn up most in film and television subtitles

intro.heading: Gender lives in the word, not in the thing
body: German gender is not a fact about the object. "das Mädchen" is a girl and neuter; "der Löffel" and "die Gabel" lie side by side on the same table. Searching the meaning for a reason is the one approach that is guaranteed to fail, and most people spend a while doing it anyway.

What does predict gender is the shape of the word, and above all its ending. A handful of endings are close to exceptionless, and they cover a real slice of the language -- for those words, gender stops being something you remember and becomes something you can see.

The rest have to be learned one at a time, which is what this deck is for. The one habit worth forming: learn a word as "die Tür", never as "Tür, feminine". The article is part of the word, not a label attached to it afterwards -- and that is also how you will need it when you start declining things.

groups.label: Feminine -- the most predictable of the three
groups.hook: These are as near exceptionless as German gets: every -ung, every -heit, every -keit is feminine, without exception worth mentioning. Nouns ending in -e are usually feminine too, but that one is a tendency rather than a rule -- der Name, der Junge and das Ende are all common words that break it.

groups.label: Masculine
groups.members: -ling, -ismus, -ant, -ent, -or, and -er when it means someone who does something
groups.hook: Days, months and seasons are masculine as a block -- der Montag, der Mai, der Sommer -- and so are the compass points. Be careful with -er: it is reliable for people (der Fahrer, der Lehrer) and says nothing whatever about things (das Fenster, das Wasser, die Mutter, die Butter).

groups.label: Neuter
groups.hook: -chen and -lein beat everything else, which is exactly why das Mädchen is neuter. Any infinitive used as a noun is neuter too, with no exceptions at all: das Essen, das Leben, das Lernen. Watch two traps -- der Moment is the -ment that got away, and the native -ling is masculine (der Frühling) where the borrowed -ing is not (das Training).

intro.closing: Stuck with nothing to go on? Guess der. It is the most common answer in this deck, at roughly two in five -- but only just ahead of die, so treat it as a tie-breaker and not a strategy. The endings above are where the real winnings are.
